source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension (នាយកដ្ឋានផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម) - "ដំណាំក្រូចពោធិសាត់" (Pursat Orange Cultivation Guide), 2016, 26pp
text:
The source describes three main ways farmers can produce Pursat orange planting material (បច្ចេកទេសរៀបចំពូជ):

1. Seed propagation (ការបង្កាត់ដោយគ្រាប់ / Seed Propagation) - growing new trees directly from seed. This is the simplest method but is not commonly recommended for commercial planting, because seedling trees can vary genetically from the parent tree and generally take longer - about 4 to 5 years - before they begin to bear fruit.

2. Air-layering / marcotting (Microstiing) - a technique many Cambodian farmers are familiar with, in which a section of a healthy branch is encouraged to grow its own roots while still attached to the parent tree, then cut off and planted separately. This method reproduces the parent tree's characteristics faithfully and can bear fruit sooner than seed-grown trees.

3. Grafting and budding (Grafting) - joining a bud or scion (មេក) from a good mother tree onto a separate rootstock (ដើមគល់). This is the method most recommended by agricultural extension workers, because grafted trees combine a strong, well-adapted root system with fruiting wood known to be productive and true-to-type.
